 Tax refunds help local families cover bills; GRABC seeks volunteers to support that work
 For many families served by Green River Asset Building Coalition, a tax refund helps pay bills, reduce debt, or establish savings. As the nonprofit prepares for the 2027 filing season, it needs more volunteers to help Daviess County residents access free tax preparation.
 RR Ryan Richardson November 19, 2026 · 12:13 am · Updated 1:31 am · 3 min read 
 Letter 8.5 × 11 in Legal 8.5 × 14 in Tabloid 11 × 17 in 
 File photo by Ryan Richardson 
 For many families served by Green River Asset Building Coalition, a tax refund helps pay bills, reduce debt, or establish savings. As the nonprofit prepares for the 2027 filing season, it needs more volunteers to help Daviess County residents access free tax preparation.
 A voluntary survey during the 2026 filing season found that 42% of responding GRABC taxpayers planned to use their refunds to pay bills or reduce debt, while 24% intended to start saving.
 Advertisement 
 Executive Director Carolyn Ferber said the service helps families avoid tax preparation costs while claiming available credits and deductions.
 According to United for ALICE figures cited by GRABC, 41% of Daviess County households were below the ALICE threshold in 2024. That includes households living in poverty and those classified as Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed — households earning above the poverty level but struggling to afford basic expenses. Statewide, the figure was 43%.
 “With these statistics, and our economic environment today, these families need more help than before, not only to save on tax filing costs, but to also ensure they are maximizing all available tax credits and deductions for that much needed tax refund,” Ferber said.
 GRABC is recruiting volunteers for its Daviess County Volunteer Income Tax Assistance site before the filing season begins in late January. No tax preparation experience is required, and training and ongoing support are provided.
 “Many people express doubt, even anxiety at the thought of doing someone’s tax return,” Ferber said. “Whether it’s a lack of experience, or an ominous-sounding task, we support new volunteers with training and IRS-certified materials along with ongoing support throughout the season.”
 The organization welcomes volunteers from a variety of backgrounds and offers flexible scheduling during weekday and Saturday operating hours.
 Prospective volunteers can learn more during a recruitment information session Thursday, Dec. 3, at 11:30 a.m. Contact GRABC for location details and information about getting started.
 GRABC and its volunteer team have provided free tax preparation since 2004. The program serves qualifying low- to moderate-income households, seniors, people with disabilities, and taxpayers with limited English proficiency.
 Supporters include IRS VITA grants, the Hager Foundation, Daviess County Fiscal Court, and United Way Ohio Valley. The nonprofit has one paid staff position, with volunteers carrying out the rest of its work.
 “This effort is truly dependent on the community’s support of their time and energy,” Ferber said.
 For more information about volunteering or the Dec. 3 session, call 270-685-1603, email [email protected] , or visit grabc.org .
